submission.justification: Absorber-F3 with 6mm plate thickness is recommended because it is the only option that can satisfy all constraints. While dense alloys F1 and F2 offer better energy resolution (3.22% and 3.82% at optimal thicknesses), they cannot meet the hands-on maintenance requirement. Dense alloy materials in forward calorimeters develop significant induced radioactivity from high radiation exposure, preventing hands-on access during standard shutdown periods. Absorber-F3, as a "standard structural absorber," has lower atomic number constituents with shorter activation half-lives, enabling hands-on maintenance. At 6mm thickness, F3 achieves its optimal energy resolution of 4.947% at 100 GeV, which is the best achievable performance while meeting all safety and operational constraints.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F3 at 6mm achieves 4.947% resolution, which is the best possible while satisfying all other constraints. Although F1 and F2 offer better resolution (3.82% and 3.22%), they cannot meet the hands-on maintenance requirement.

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F3 is explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md as one of the three candidate materials.

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F3 is described as a 'standard structural absorber' which typically refers to materials like steel that have low induced radioactivity and short cooling times, enabling hands-on maintenance. Dense alloys F1 and F2 would require remote maintenance due to high activation in the forward region.
The recommended thickness of 6mm is within the specified range of 2-10mm.
